clue.text: Scotsman and his flash masculine pride

parts.note: Mac is a familiar way of addressing a Scotsman
a flash is a moment, abbreviated MO

explanation.surface: A Scot and his swagger are both showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is an exaggerated sense of manliness and pride in it.

clue.text: Hot water bottles a good vision

indicators.note: bottles means contains, so the trouble word holds the rest

parts.note: to be in hot water is to be in the mire, in trouble

explanation.surface: A hot-water bottle offering a pleasant sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, something seen that is not there.

clue.text: Line written up about fool and prophetess

indicators.note: about means the line goes around the other pieces
in a down clue, written up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an arc is a curved line
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A written line about a fool and a prophetess, like a myth summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' reverses only the line, which then goes 'about' the fool and the word 'and', taken as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra was the Trojan seer fated never to be believed.

clue.text: 'I' in 'ego' up first

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top
in means the letter is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, read as Latin I

explanation.surface: A grammar note about the letter I inside the word ego.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ego' stands for LATIN I (its translation is Latin I); I goes in to make LAITINI, and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means at the beginning, coming first.

clue.text: Necessary figure about which I'm astonished!

indicators.note: about means the exclamation surrounds the figure

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of astonishment
one is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A vital number that leaves the speaker amazed.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The necessary' is British slang for the cash needed for something.

clue.text: Very many lackeys lacking leadership

indicators.note: losing the leading letter of the word for lackeys

parts.note: poodles are servile followers, lapdogs

explanation.surface: A boss surrounded by crowds of yes-men who have no one in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a large quantity, lots and lots.

clue.text: Source of great wealth, painting skilfully

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting
well means competently

explanation.surface: An artist's skilled work proves a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A productive petroleum bore can make its owner very rich.

clue.text: Flower anyone can see in a large bunch

indicators.note: in means the certificate letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: lots is a large number
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, open to all

explanation.surface: A flower visible to all in a big bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the UK film rating meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a flowering plant.

clue.text: Comprehensive school's principal visibly upset

indicators.note: principal means the leading letter of the word school

parts.note: weeping is shedding tears, upset for all to see

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school's head is seen to be distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive school' looks like a phrase; 'Comprehensive' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping means wide-ranging, all-embracing.

clue.text: Officer left mostly with pink clothing!

indicators.note: clothing means the colour wraps around the other piece

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour

indicators.note: mostly means losing the final letter

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: An officer leaving, dressed in pink, which is surprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a non-commissioned army rank.

clue.text: Game over if one hasn't drawn a blank?

definitions.text: Game over if one hasn't drawn a blank?

parts.words: Game over if one hasn't drawn a blank?
parts.note: in the deadly revolver game, drawing an empty chamber is the lucky outcome; anything else ends play for good

explanation.surface: Sounds like a lottery or quiz where failing to draw a blank card loses.
explanation.definitionFit: The deadly gamble with a revolver holding one bullet: a live chamber ends the game and the player.

clue.text: It's gone in the sauce? That's a downer!

indicators.note: has gone in means the first piece is placed inside the sauce

parts.note: gravy is a meat sauce
the word It, with 's read as 'has'

explanation.surface: Something has fallen into the gravy, which is a let-down.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'It's gone in' as 'It has gone in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravity is the force that pulls everything down, so it is literally a downer.

clue.text: Exercise getting journalists out of bed

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively
up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: Reporters dragging themselves out of bed is a workout in itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up is a floor exercise pushing the body up with the arms.

clue.text: I procrastinate, perhaps, as a devotee

parts.note: to say 'do later' is one way of procrastinating

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they put things off, presented as a sort of devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater is a worshipper, hence a devoted follower or fan.

clue.text: A must, I suspect, to eat Irish dessert

indicators.note: eating means the jumbled letters take in the other piece
suspect as an adjective means dodgy, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insisting an Irish dessert is a must.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian layered pudding of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone.

clue.text: Light colour that doesn't work

definitions.meaning: a dud or useless thing, as with a faulty car

explanation.surface: A pale shade that fails to suit, or a lamp that will not switch on.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon is a pale yellow, and slang for a defective item, especially a car.

clue.text: Maine's not bad for a US state

indicators.note: bad means the letters have gone wrong, rearranged

explanation.surface: Maine is not a bad choice of US state.
explanation.walkthrough: Maine is a US state too, the obvious false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is a Midwestern American state.

clue.text: Thus dressing doctor in yellow, not entirely representative

indicators.note: dressing means clothing, wrapping around the rest

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus

indicators.note: in means the doctor goes inside
not entirely means losing the last letter

parts.note: the yolk is the yellow of an egg
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A doctor in yellow dressing, only partly representative.
explanation.definitionFit: Symbolic means standing for something, emblematic.

clue.text: Rear of cavity bearing fungus

indicators.note: rear means the last letter of the word cavity

parts.note: east is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Fungus growing at the back of a hollow, perhaps in a tooth or wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is a single-celled fungus used in brewing and baking.

clue.text: Thump counter in a frenzy

indicators.note: wild agitation suggests the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Banging a shop counter in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce is to beat soundly, to thrash.

clue.text: Appropriate payment including European currency, Austrian capital

indicators.note: including means the payment holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: rent is a regular payment
the lev is Bulgaria's currency

indicators.note: capital means the first, capital letter of Austrian

explanation.surface: A fitting fee involving a European currency and Vienna.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Austrian capital' looks like Vienna but means just its first letter, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevant means pertinent or applicable, a synonym of appropriate.

clue.text: Experienced apostle's heading off in front

indicators.note: in means the trimmed name goes inside

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard

indicators.note: the apostle's name has its head, the leading letter, cut off

parts.note: Peter is an apostle; the 's is read as 'has'

explanation.surface: An apostle sets off at the head of a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is a person with long experience; used as an adjective, seasoned.

clue.text: Pickled — like a plum?

definitions.meaning: slang for drunk, or high on drugs
a ... plum has its stone removed

explanation.surface: Is a pickled plum drunk?
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned means intoxicated, and fruit with the pit taken out is stoned.

clue.text: Good time to put away red pants in private chamber

indicators.note: putting away means the good time swallows the jumbled letters

parts.note: a boom is a time of prosperity

indicators.note: pants as a verb in British slang means is rubbish, signalling a messed-up rearrangement

explanation.surface: Stashing red underwear somewhere private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear but is British slang for rubbish, here the anagram signal on 'red'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom is a private room for sleeping.

clue.text: Very old, extremely upset about end of contract

indicators.note: about means the turned word surrounds the letter
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down

parts.note: dead means utterly, as in dead easy

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word contract

explanation.surface: Someone ancient, much troubled by a contract ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated means old-fashioned, belonging to a past era.

clue.text: Obvious one needs nursing?

indicators.note: nursing means holding inside, so obvious must hold one

parts.note: patent means plain or evident
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Plainly this person requires care.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a person who obviously needs nursing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital case under medical care is someone requiring nursing.

clue.text: Put map on top of table

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram
T is the abbreviation for table

explanation.surface: Lay the map on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant is to place or set something firmly.

clue.text: Party beaten, I won and lost here

indicators.note: beaten as in whisked or battered into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports report: the side was beaten, yet I won and lost here.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax and enjoy oneself without restraint, as at a party, is the idiom.

clue.text: Club something to chew on, then stick

parts.note: cud is food a cow chews again
to gel is to stick together or set

explanation.surface: Chewing something, then sticking, with a club in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A cudgel is a short heavy stick used as a weapon.

clue.text: Typical colours, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a regimental flag or banner, carried as colours

explanation.surface: Is this the usual set of colours?
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means normal, and a standard is a flag, as regimental colours are.
